PSEUDO-JUBILEES — COMPLETE TEXT

FRAGMENT 1 — THE AQEDAH — 4Q225 Fragment 2

1 [And YHWH tested Avraham with a tenth test saying:] Take your son Yitzhak and go to the land of Moriyah and offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains that I will show you.

2 And Mastemah came before YHWH and accused Avraham saying: He loves his son more than he loves You. Test him. Command him to offer the boy and you will see whether he will obey You or whether his love for his son is greater.

3 And Avraham rose early in the morning and saddled his donkey and took Yitzhak his son and two young men and the wood and he went to the place that YHWH had commanded him.

4 And on the third day Avraham lifted up his eyes and saw the place from far away. And he said to the young men: Stay here with the donkey and I and the boy will go there and worship and we will return to you.

5 And Avraham took the fire and the knife and they went together. And Yitzhak said: Here is the fire and the wood but where is the lamb for the burnt offering? And Avraham said: YHWH will provide the lamb, my son.

6 And when Avraham stretched out his hand to take the knife, the angel of YHWH called to him from the heavens and said: Do not lay your hand on the boy. For now I know that you fear YHWH more than anything, for you did not withhold your son from me.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] 4Q225 Fragment 2 contains the most detailed Aqedah account outside the Masoretic Bereshit. The Pseudo-Jubilees version explicitly names Mastemah as the accuser who prompted the test — a detail present also in the Orit Ge'ez Yovelim 17:16 but absent from the Masoretic Bereshit 22. This confirms that the Mastemah tradition is ancient and not a later addition.

[ORIT GE'EZ] The Orit Ge'ez Yovelim 17-18 contains the fullest version of this Mastemah-Aqedah tradition. The Pseudo-Jubilees text and the Ge'ez Yovelim share the Mastemah detail and other elements, confirming that both draw on a common ancient Hebrew/Aramaic tradition that the Masoretic account condensed. The Ge'ez preserves the fuller original form.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] The Masoretic Bereshit 22 contains no mention of Mastemah or any accuser figure. YHWH simply decides to test Avraham. The Pseudo-Jubilees and Orit Ge'ez Yovelim tradition, which includes Mastemah's role, represents an older and theologically more complete account: the test arises from a challenge in the divine court, not from an arbitrary divine decision.

[CRITICAL NOTE] The Mastemah detail in the Aqedah tradition is theologically significant in ways Western scholarship has largely avoided. If the test of Avraham was prompted by a challenge in the divine court, then the Aqedah is not a test of Avraham's obedience for YHWH's benefit — YHWH already knows what Avraham will do. It is a demonstration to the divine court, specifically to the accusing spirit, that YHWH's chosen one is faithful. This completely changes the theological meaning of the event.

FRAGMENT 2 — CHANOKH TRADITIONS — 4Q227 Fragment 2

1 [And Chanokh walked with the angels of The Creator for six jubilees of years. And they showed him everything that is in the heavens and on the earth and in the deep places below the earth and in the hidden places.]

2 And Chanokh wrote everything in a book and he gave the book to his son Metushelah saying: Guard this book and give it to your children after you for generation upon generation. For it contains the wisdom of the ages and the mystery of all creation.

3 And Chanokh was with the angels of The Creator and he was not with men after that. For The Creator took him and he was no more seen among the children of men. But his writings remained and his wisdom endured.

4 And Metushelah kept the book of his father Chanokh and he read it all the days of his life. And in the days of Noach he gave it to him saying: In the days that are coming you will need the wisdom that is in this book. Guard it and teach it to your children.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] 4Q227 Fragment 2 preserves the Chanokh tradition in a Hebrew form distinct from the Aramaic Chanokh corpus. The reference to Chanokh writing everything in a book and entrusting it to Metushelah parallels Chanokh 81-82 in the Orit Ge'ez version. This confirms that the Chanokh book-transmission tradition existed in Hebrew as well as Aramaic, confirming its ancient and widespread nature.

[ORIT GE'EZ] The Orit Ge'ez Chanokh 81-82 describes in detail Chanokh's instruction to Metushelah to guard and transmit his writings. The Pseudo-Jubilees fragment preserves this same tradition in Hebrew, confirming that the Ge'ez version is not a late development but preserves an ancient tradition also attested at Qumran.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] The Masoretic Bereshit 5:24 records only that Chanokh walked with YHWH and was no more because YHWH took him. No mention of writing, no mention of transmitted wisdom, no mention of the book tradition. The Pseudo-Jubilees and Orit Ge'ez traditions preserve the fuller account that the Masoretic canonical process reduced to a single verse.

[CRITICAL NOTE] The transmission chain of Chanokh's wisdom — from Chanokh to Metushelah to Noach — is a statement about the continuity of revealed wisdom through the pre-flood period. The flood does not destroy the wisdom tradition because it has been entrusted to the righteous line in written form. This is a theology of textual preservation as divine strategy, which is highly significant for understanding the Qumran community's own self-understanding as the guardians of the true textual tradition.
